This is the chargesheet submitted by the Psi of
Yelahanka Police Station against the accused persons
for the offences punishable U/s.468, 471, 420 r/w 34
of I.P.C.
 3 C.C.No. 20101/2016
2.

The case of the prosecution is that, the accused
No.1 was the owner of house property bearing Khatha
No.277/159/12 of Venkatala Village situated within
the jurisdiction of Yelahanka Police Station, he sold it
to Cw.1 through sale deed dated 02.12.2004.

Thereafter, the accused No.1 along with his wife
accused No.2, in furtherance of common intention to
cheat Cw.1, crated alleged Gpa said to be executed by

Cw.1 and based on that sold said house property to
Cw.2 and thereby the accused have committed the
offences punishable under section 468, 471, 420 r/w
34 of I.P.C.

2

 3.
The accused are on bail.

As required u/sec.
207 of Cr.PC,

the copies of the charge sheet papers
were furnished to the accused.

Charge was framed for
the offences punishable U/s. 468, 471, 420 r/w 34 of
I.P.C. and read over and explained to the accused in
the language known to them.
Accused have not
pleaded guilty and claimed for trial.

The prosecution in order to prove its case, has
examined PWs.1 to 5 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 3.

On
closure of the evidence on the side of the prosecution,
the statement of the accused u/sec. 313 Cr.PC came
to be recorded, the accused have denied the
incriminating evidence appearing against them and not
chosen to lead defense evidence.
5. Heard the arguments.

Perused the documents
placed on record.

6. The points that arise for consideration are :
 1. Whether the prosecution
 has proves beyond all
 reasonable doubt that accused
 have committed the offences
 U/s 468, 471, 420 r/w 34 of
I.P.C. ?
 2. What order ?
 5 C.C.No. 20101/2016
Shivkumar vs Muttuswamy.B on 10 July, 2025

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171222501/
3

 7.

The above points are answered as under :
 Point No.1: In the Negative
 Point No.2: As per final order
 for the following :
 Reasons
8. Point No.1 : That the accused No.1 is owner of
house property bearing Khatha No.277/159/12 of
Venkatala Village, he sold it to Cw.1 through sale deed
dated 02.12.2004. Thereafter, the accused No.1 along
with his wife accused No.2, in furtherance of common
intention to cheat Cw.1, crated alleged Gpa said to be
executed by Cw.1 and based on that, sold said house
property to Cw.2 and thereby the accused have
committed the offences punishable under section 468,
471, 420 r/w 34 of I.P.C.
 9.

The Ld. Sr.APP for the state during the course of
argument has submitted that prosecution has
examined complaint, eye witnesses and police official
 6 C.C.No. 20101/2016
witnesses as Pw.1 to 5, though the rest of the
witnesses did not turn up, the evidence placed by
prosecution through official witnesses and
documentary evidence are clearly establishes that the
accused have committed the offense as alleged in the
charge sheet.

Therefore, prays to convict the accused
Shivkumar vs Muttuswamy.B on 10 July, 2025
Indian

Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171222501/
4

by imposing maximum sentence.

10. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for
accused has submitted that though the prosecution
infromant as Pw.1, eye witnesses examined as Pw.2
and 3 and they deposed asserting the version of
prosecution case in thier examination in chief

, they did
not turn up for cross examination, when they are not
subject to cross examination, their evidence does not
have any sanctity under law of evidence.
Pw.4 and 5

are the police officials, naturally they deposed in
support of prosecution case as they being police
officials.

In the absance of the evidence of material
 7 C.C.No. 20101/2016
witnesses, the evidence of police officials is of no use.

Therefore, the accused are entitled to benefit of doubt
and prays for acquit the accused.

11. In the light of the submission made above, on
careful perusal of oral and documentary evidence
placed by the prosecution, as rightly pointed out by
the learned counsel for accused

, in the examination-
in-chief, Pw.1 informant and Pw.2 and 3 eye witnesses
have deposed about how the accused have sold the
house property to Pw.2 belongs to Pw.1 creating Gpa
said to be executed by Pw.1 and how Pw.2 purchased
Shivkumar vs Muttuswamy.B on 10 July, 2025
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171222501/
5

said house from accused.

Thereafter, when the case
was deferred for their cross examination, despite
issued warrants and proclamation, they did not turn
up, hence they have been dropped.

The law is very
clear that, when witness did not avail for his cross
examination, the evidence adduced by such witness by
way of examination-in-chef, has no evidentiary value.
 8 C.C.No. 20101/2016

Here, in this case, Pw.1 to 3 did turn turn up for cross
examination despite taken coercive steps against them,
hence, in view of settled position of law stated
aforesaid, the evidence of Pw.1 to 3 has no evidentiary
value under Evidence Act.

Further, Pw.4 and 5 are the
police officials and deposed with regard to official act
done by them during the course of investigation.

They
are police officials, they deposed regarding what is
their role during the course of investigation, naturally
they supported the prosecution case as they being
police officials.

In spite of repeated warrants and Nbw,
the other witnesses did not turn up to adduce
evidence.

So, in the absence of evidence of material
witnesses, the evidence of police officials is of no use to
prove the offence alleged against the accused.

12. Therefore, in view of discussion made above, the
considered opinion is of the court that, the prosecution
Shivkumar vs Muttuswamy.B on 10 July, 2025
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171222501/
6

has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond
 9 C.C.No. 20101/2016
reasonable doubt.

The accused are entitled to benefit
of doubt.

Hence, answered the point No.1 in the
Negative.
13. Point No.2:

In view of discussion made on
point No.1 this court proceeds to pass following
 Order
Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C the accused are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable
under sections 468, 471, 420 r/w 34 of I.P.C.
Bail bonds of accused and their surety bond stands cance
lled after six months from today.
